title: User Embeddings are Superpositions of Interpretable Behavioral Modes
headline: Interpretable User Embeddings: Sparse Superpositions of Behavioral Modes
tldr: User embeddings can be decomposed into a sparse mix of interpretable behavioral modes, enhancing transparency in recommendation systems. This approach preserves predictive power while offering clear insights into user behavior.
significance: It bridges the gap between dense embedding representations and human-understandable behavioral patterns, improving trust and explainability in AI systems.

title: Do You Miss the Nights We Spent Crafting Figures? Rethinking Teaser and Framework Figures in the Age of Generative AI
headline: Reimagining Scientific Figures with Generative AI: A Visual Retrospective
tldr: The study analyzes 371 motivation and framework figures from 200 papers to assess how generative AI reshapes visual clarity and expression. It highlights both opportunities and challenges in using AI to design scientific visuals.
significance: It offers a systematic evaluation of AI’s impact on scientific communication, guiding future figure design practices.

title: EgoGeneralist: Unifying Egocentric Action-Video Tasks through Video-Native Modeling
headline: EgoGeneralist Unifies Egocentric Video Generation, Pose Estimation, and Action Modeling
tldr: EgoGeneralist adapts pretrained video generators to create action-conditioned egocentric videos and estimate pose in a single framework. Its role‑adaptive action renderer offers video‑native 3D representations for multidirectional action learning.
significance: It bridges multiple egocentric video tasks into a unified, video‑native model, enhancing efficiency and consistency across generation and perception.

title: An Accelerated Proximal Gradient Method for Bures-Wasserstein Space
headline: Accelerated Proximal Gradient Method for Efficient Bures–Wasserstein Space Optimization in Gaussian Measures
tldr: We propose lifting Bures–Wasserstein problems to Euclidean space of affine transport maps, enabling accelerated proximal gradient solutions. This yields faster convergence for composite optimization of Gaussian measures.
significance: The method dramatically speeds up optimization in Bures–Wasserstein space, opening new possibilities for efficient Gaussian measure computations.

title: Canonical Cut Hierarchy in Almost-Linear Time via Reduction to Max-Flow
headline: Fast Canonical Cut Hierarchy via Max-Flow Reduction Algorithm
tldr: We present a randomized almost linear-time algorithm for computing the canonical cut hierarchy in undirected graphs with polynomially bounded capacities by reducing the problem to max-flow. This approach yields efficient algorithms for related partitioning tasks.
significance: This work provides the first near-linear time method for constructing canonical cut hierarchies, enabling faster graph partitioning in large-scale networks.

title: Towards interpreting any residual stream direction by scaling activation inversion
headline: Decoding Residual Stream Directions for Any Language Model via Activation Inversion
tldr: The paper introduces Maximally-Activating Example Metamodels (MAEMs) that map residual stream directions to text exemplars, enabling interpretation beyond corpus limits. By scaling activation inversion, it provides a systematic way to understand internal representations of language models.
significance: This method offers a practical framework for interpreting the abstract directions within large language models, enhancing transparency and trust.

title: OopsieRecover: Learning Transferable VLA Corrections from Semantic Interventions
headline: OopsieRecover: Teaching Vision‑Language‑Action Models to Self‑Correct via Semantic Interventions for Robotic Manipulation
tldr: OopsieRecover learns transferable corrections for Vision‑Language‑Action models by using semantic interventions, enabling robots to recover from failures without extensive corrective data. The method generalizes across tasks, reducing the need for task‑specific fine‑tuning.
significance: It dramatically lowers the data cost for deploying robust VLA robots in real‑world settings.

title: Quantum Knowledge Distillation: State-of-the-art, Applications and Open Problems
headline: Quantum Knowledge Distillation: Advancing Model Compression and Cross-Architecture Transfer
tldr: This survey explores quantum knowledge distillation techniques, covering state-of-the-art methods, diverse applications, and open research challenges. It highlights how quantum-derived supervision can compress models, enable cross-architecture transfer, and facilitate classical deployment.
significance: Quantum knowledge distillation bridges quantum and classical learning, offering scalable, efficient solutions for complex AI tasks.

title: Latent RL Priors for Data-Efficient Dexterous Manipulation
headline: Data-Efficient Dexterous Manipulation via Latent Reinforcement Learning Priors from Visual Demonstrations
tldr: We introduce Latent RL Prior, a two-stage framework that first learns rich control behaviors in simulation with privileged information, then transfers this knowledge to real-world dexterous manipulation using a latent representation. The approach dramatically reduces the number of visual demonstrations needed while maintaining precise control.
significance: This work bridges simulation-based RL and real-world manipulation, enabling efficient learning from limited visual data and advancing the practicality of dexterous robotic systems.

title: Adversarial Training with Large Step Sizes: Implicit Bias, Optimization, and Sharpness
headline: Large Step Sizes in Adversarial Training: Bias, Optimization, and Sharpness Dynamics
tldr: The paper analyzes deterministic gradient descent with large step sizes in adversarial training, uncovering how such steps influence implicit bias and loss landscape sharpness. It provides practical insights that enable faster convergence while maintaining robustness.
significance: This work bridges theory and practice by showing how large step sizes shape robustness and convergence in adversarial training, guiding more efficient training strategies.

title: Cognitive Tours: Making Understanding a Deliverable in AI-Assisted Development
headline: Cognitive and Intent Debt: Hidden Risks in AI-Accelerated Software Development
tldr: Generative AI and agentic coding speed up development but can erode shared understanding, creating cognitive debt. Intent debt arises when the original purpose of code is unclear, threatening long-term maintainability.
significance: Recognizing and addressing these debts is essential to sustain healthy, adaptable software ecosystems.

title: Unpacking the Compute Efficiency of Strong-to-Weak OPD against GRPO
headline: Compute Efficiency of OPD vs GRPO: A Systematic Comparison in RL
tldr: We systematically compare vanilla reverse‑KL OPD with Group Relative Policy Optimization across task difficulty, model size, and domain. The results indicate that OPD’s dense teacher signal can cut training FLOPs while achieving comparable accuracy.
significance: It demonstrates that on‑policy distillation can be a more compute‑efficient alternative to RL for training language models.

title: ReproBridge: Building Reproducibility into ML Research Artifacts
headline: ReproBridge: Enhancing ML Experiment Reproducibility with Recovered Procedures and Decisions
tldr: ReproBridge reconstructs missing experimental details from papers and code, enabling coding agents to reproduce ML studies more reliably. Our evaluation shows that preserving these recovered procedures boosts independent replication success.
significance: This work demonstrates that systematic recovery of experimental workflows can substantially improve reproducibility in machine learning research.

title: BeAR: The Bern Atmospheric Retrieval code - A GPU-accelerated framework for low-resolution, high-resolution, and joint retrievals of exoplanet atmospheres
headline: GPU-Accelerated BeAR: Joint Retrieval of Exoplanet Atmospheres in Low and High Resolution
tldr: BeAR extends Helios-r with a GPU-accelerated framework that jointly analyzes low- and high-resolution spectra using cross‑correlation log‑likelihoods. It enables rapid, unified retrievals of exoplanet atmospheric properties from diverse data sets.
significance: BeAR delivers the first real‑time, joint retrieval tool for exoplanet atmospheres, combining low‑ and high‑resolution data to improve compositional constraints.

title: Provable circuit-level thresholds for non-abelian topological phases
headline: Explicit Circuit-Level Thresholds for Non-Abelian Topological Quantum Memory in 2D Systems
tldr: We construct syndrome extraction circuits using the Turaev-Viro path integral and a classical decoding algorithm that operates online. The scheme achieves a provable error threshold under local stochastic circuit-level noise, enabling robust quantum memory in any 2D non-chiral topological order.
significance: This work provides the first rigorous threshold proof for fault-tolerant quantum memories in non-abelian topological phases, paving the way for scalable quantum computing.

title: Where and Why is Grounded Reasoning Useful?
headline: Grounded Reasoning: Identifying When It Works Best in Visual Tasks
tldr: Grounded reasoning, which outputs coordinate hints during chain-of-thought, improves visual problem solving. This study quantifies its benefits and limits across tasks.
significance: Understanding grounded reasoning guides the design of more effective AI models for visual reasoning.

title: Evolution of Dust In Protoplanetary Disks With Magnetized Winds
headline: Dust Dynamics in Magnetized Protoplanetary Disk Winds: Implications for Planet Formation
tldr: Recent studies suggest magnetized winds dominate angular momentum transport in weakly turbulent disks, yet the resulting dust evolution remains unclear. Understanding whether these winds can generate dust-rich regions is crucial for planet formation theories.
significance: This work bridges disk wind dynamics and dust aggregation, offering new insights into how planets may form in magnetically influenced environments.

title: SwarmEvolve: Latent Agent Swarms for Evolutionary Discovery and Optimization
headline: SwarmEvolve: Using Latent Agent Swarms to Speed Up LLM-Driven Evolutionary Optimization
tldr: SwarmEvolve introduces a framework that employs latent agent swarms to accelerate LLM-guided evolutionary search, reducing the need for repetitive chain-of-thought generation. By maintaining population diversity through agent collaboration, it speeds up optimization for mathematical and computational problems.
significance: This approach dramatically improves the efficiency of AI-driven program synthesis, enabling faster discovery of high-performing solutions.

title: Joint analysis of the Macquart relation and the dispersion measure power spectrum: cross-covariance and redshift self-calibration
headline: Joint Analysis of Macquart Relation and DM Power Spectrum: Cross-Covariance and Redshift Self-Calibration
tldr: The study derives the cross-covariance between the DM-redshift (Macquart) relation and the angular power spectrum of dispersion measures from FRBs, enabling simultaneous constraints on ionised baryons and redshift calibration. This combined approach improves the precision of cosmological and feedback models using FRB data.
significance: It provides a unified framework to extract cosmological information from FRB observations, enhancing our understanding of baryonic distribution and feedback processes.

title: Scientist World: Grow a Research World for AI-Scientists
headline: Scientist World: Turning Research Papers into Executable Environments for AI Scientists
tldr: We create a platform that transforms scientific literature into runnable code, enabling AI agents to experiment directly with research findings. Our autonomous pipeline parses papers, extracts models and data, and deploys them as interactive environments.
significance: This bridges the gap between static scientific knowledge and dynamic AI experimentation, accelerating discovery.

title: Direct transition from a fractional Chern insulator to a topological superconductor
headline: Direct Transition from Fractional Chern Insulator to Topological Superconductor in a Chern Band
tldr: Numerical simulations reveal a continuous phase transition between a Laughlin fractional Chern insulator and a c_- = 3/2 topological superconductor as bandwidth increases at ν=1/3. The critical point shows diverging electron correlation length at momenta away from the Fermi surface, suggesting a novel universality class.
significance: This work uncovers a new route to topological superconductivity and deepens understanding of quantum phase transitions in strongly correlated systems.

title: XStack: A Benchmark for ML Repo Migration
headline: XStack: Benchmarking Cross-Framework ML Repository Migration Between PyTorch and JAX
tldr: XStack provides a standardized benchmark for migrating machine learning repositories between PyTorch and JAX, enabling researchers to test and validate code across different hardware platforms. The framework automates building, testing, and performance comparison, making it easier to unlock new hardware capabilities.
significance: By facilitating seamless migration, XStack expands research flexibility and accelerates the adoption of diverse hardware accelerators.

title: Joint Electricity Price and Load Forecasting for Data Center Battery Dispatch Using Polynomial Diffusion Models
headline: Real-Time Battery Dispatch for Data Centers Using Polynomial Diffusion Forecasts
tldr: The paper introduces a real-time dispatch framework that leverages polynomial diffusion models to jointly forecast electricity prices and data center load. By predicting both variables, the system optimally schedules battery energy storage to shift consumption from high-price to low-price periods, reducing operating costs.
significance: It demonstrates how advanced stochastic modeling can directly improve energy efficiency and cost savings in large-scale data centers.

title: Same Behavior, Different Mechanism: What Finite Experiments Can Certify About Integrated Information
headline: Finite Experiments and Integrated Information: Certifying Mechanisms in AI Systems
tldr: The paper investigates whether finite, noisy experiments can identify causal mechanisms underlying integrated information. It shows that certain mechanism-level quantities are continuous and identifiable under realistic experimental constraints.
significance: It provides a theoretical foundation for reliable AI auditing by linking experimental observables to internal causal structure.

title: From Pixels to Actions - Towards Native Vision-Language-Action Policies
headline: From Pixels to Actions: Rethinking Vision-Language-Action Policy Design for Robotic Manipulation Tasks
tldr: Vision-language-action models typically compress perception before reasoning, but manipulation depends on fine-grained visual cues. This work proposes native policies that directly integrate raw visual signals into action decision-making.
significance: By preserving low-level visual details, the proposed approach enables more precise and responsive robotic manipulation.

title: Using topology to reveal all mutually unbiased bases in dimension six
headline: Topology Uncovers All Mutually Unbiased Bases in Six-Dimensional Quantum Space
tldr: Researchers used topological analysis of complex Hadamard matrices to prove that no fourth mutually unbiased basis exists in dimension six. This resolves a 30-year open question in quantum information theory.
significance: The result settles a long-standing problem, confirming that the maximum number of mutually unbiased bases in six dimensions is three.

title: ReveaLLAGN 3: Revealing the Infrared Spectral Energy Distributions of Low Luminosity AGN
headline: JWST Unveils Infrared SEDs of Seven Nearby Low-Luminosity AGNs
tldr: Using JWST, researchers mapped the near- to mid-infrared spectral energy distributions of seven low-luminosity active galactic nuclei, separating the AGN component from host galaxy light. The study provides new insights into the emission mechanisms in the innermost regions of faint AGNs.
significance: This work demonstrates JWST’s capability to disentangle AGN emission in the infrared, advancing our understanding of low-luminosity AGN physics.

title: Preparing for the Gaia DR4 Epochalypse: Simulated Epoch Astrometry for Substellar Companion Orbit-Modeling Benchmarks
headline: Simulating Gaia DR4 Epoch Astrometry to Benchmark Substellar Companion Orbit Models
tldr: Gaia DR4 will deliver epoch astrometry for billions of stars, enabling the discovery of thousands of substellar companions. We provide a simulated catalog of Gaia-like epoch data to test orbit‑modeling pipelines on a common set of injected systems.
significance: This benchmark will accelerate the development and validation of orbit‑modeling algorithms for future astrometric surveys.

title: A Framework for Context Enrichment and Selective Robustness in LLM Social Agents
headline: Enhancing Robustness of LLM Agents in Social Simulations Through Context Enrichment
tldr: The study proposes a framework that enriches contextual prompts to stabilize LLM agent behavior in social simulations. By selectively reinforcing key background cues, the approach reduces sensitivity to meaning-preserving prompt variations, addressing a key validation challenge.
significance: It offers a systematic method to improve the reliability of LLM-based agents, a critical step for deploying them in socially relevant simulations.

title: FlowReconBench: Accuracy, calibration and cost of learned and classical flow reconstruction from sparse sensors
headline: Benchmarking Learned vs Classical Flow Reconstruction from Sparse Sensors Across Reynolds Regimes
tldr: FlowReconBench evaluates ten learned and five classical methods on a laminar cylinder wake across varying Reynolds numbers and a two-dimensional flow regime, comparing accuracy, calibration, and computational cost. The study identifies conditions where data-driven models outperform traditional estimators and highlights trustworthy aspects of their predictions.
significance: This benchmark clarifies when data-driven models surpass traditional estimators and informs trustworthy deployment in fluid dynamics.

title: BEAKER: An Expert-Curated Benchmark for Embodied Brains in Self-Driving Chemical Laboratories
headline: BEAKER: Benchmarking Embodied Brains for Self‑Driving Chemical Labs
tldr: BEAKER introduces a curated benchmark for assessing multimodal large language models as embodied brains in self‑driving chemical laboratories. It evaluates perception, reasoning, and action under safety constraints, filling a gap in current laboratory benchmarks.
significance: It provides a standardized, expert‑curated testbed to advance embodied AI in chemical experimentation.

title: FrontierPhysics: Evaluating Agents for End-to-End Physics Research
headline: FrontierPhysics: New Benchmark Tests AI Agents on Real Physics Research Tasks
tldr: FrontierPhysics introduces a comprehensive end-to-end benchmark with 56 tasks crafted by 42 physicists, assessing AI agents on real research problems rather than isolated questions. It evaluates both correctness and research quality, pushing the limits of foundation models in physics.
significance: It provides the first large-scale, physics-driven benchmark that measures AI agents' ability to conduct genuine research, guiding future model development.

title: Arithmetic Depth, Minimal Gate Alphabets, and Exact Program-State Resources for Single-Qubit Dyadic Programs
headline: Exact Resource Layers for Single-Qubit Dyadic Quantum Programs
tldr: This work demonstrates that, for a single-qubit dyadic fragment, the deepest resource layer can be determined exactly rather than bounded. By leveraging the real cyclotomic tower and a normalized-midpoint misty-state syntax, the authors provide precise counts of non-Clifford gates and qubit usage.
significance: It offers a tighter, exact resource accounting for quantum circuits, improving efficiency in quantum algorithm design.

title: Perceptive Humanoid Motion from Simulation
headline: Simulated Humanoid Motion: Bridging Pixels and Joint Commands with Large-Scale Data
tldr: Researchers propose a simulation-based framework to generate paired pixel-language and joint command data for humanoid robots. This approach could accelerate generalist autonomy by providing scalable training corpora without costly human teleoperation.
significance: It addresses the critical data bottleneck hindering the development of versatile, pixel-to-joint control in humanoid robotics.

title: A Simple Subquadratic Cut Query Protocol for Directed Reachability
headline: Subquadratic Cut Query Protocol for Directed Reachability in Unweighted Graphs
tldr: The paper presents a protocol that determines if a directed path exists between two vertices using subquadratic queries to a cut oracle. It leverages submodularity of directed cut functions to reduce the query complexity of reachability problems.
significance: It advances efficient graph query algorithms by connecting reachability to submodular function query complexity.

title: Reinforcement Learning Enables Scaling Generalist Robot Policy Improvement
headline: Reinforcement Learning Drives Scalable Improvement of Generalist Robot Policies Across Domains
tldr: Reinforcement learning can iteratively refine large, generalist robot policies, enabling them to adapt to new tasks with minimal fine‑tuning. This approach leverages zero‑shot capabilities from pre‑training while scaling performance through self‑improvement cycles.
significance: It demonstrates a practical path to deploy versatile robotic systems that continuously improve without extensive task‑specific retraining.

title: Sublinear multi-type preferential attachment
headline: Sublinear Multi-Type Preferential Attachment for Community Detection in Growing Graphs
tldr: We introduce a preferential attachment model with two node types that yields sublinear degree growth. The model captures community-dependent attachment probabilities and provides analytic results on degree distributions.
significance: This work extends preferential attachment theory to heterogeneous communities, offering new insights into network evolution.

title: Motion-guided Contrastive Regularization For Latent World Models
headline: Preventing Static Collapse in JEPA-Style World Models with Motion-Guided Contrastive Regularization
tldr: JEPA-style world models learn latent dynamics without reconstructing observations, but distributional regularization alone can lead to static collapse, where the encoder preserves episode-specific static content while ignoring manipulation-relevant state changes. The authors introduce motion-guided contrastive regularization to enforce that latent representations capture dynamic changes, improving control performance.
significance: This work addresses a key failure mode in latent world models, enabling more reliable control by ensuring dynamic information is retained in the learned representations.

title: Boundary $c\leq1$ Liouville CFT from the Bootstrap
headline: Boundary Liouville CFT at c≤1: FZZT Conditions, Bootstrap, and Sewing Constraints
tldr: We construct boundary Liouville CFT with FZZT-type conditions at c≤1, deriving missing boundary three-point and bulk-to-boundary constants via analytic bootstrap. The resulting theory satisfies Cardy–Lewellen sewing constraints on the disk and annulus.
significance: This work completes the non-perturbative formulation of Liouville CFT at c≤1 with consistent boundary data, enabling further studies of 2D quantum gravity and string theory.

title: DreamX: Video Diffusion Model is a Universal Latent Action Learner
headline: DreamX: A Universal Video Diffusion Model for Action Representation Across Embodiments
tldr: DreamX learns a universal action representation by modeling consistent dynamics across different executions while remaining invariant to embodiment and appearance. Unlike prior latent action models, it disentangles action from visual noise, enabling better transfer across varied agents.
significance: This approach enables robust action transfer across diverse embodiments, advancing generalizable video understanding.

title: From Autonomous Agents to Cognitive Symbionts: Toward AI-Augmented Human Intelligence
headline: From Autonomous Agents to Cognitive Symbionts: Enhancing Human Intelligence with AI
tldr: Large foundation models now write code and run multistep tasks, and personal agents act on a person's behalf. Yet people still forget what they once knew, miss what they are not looking at, fail to find the right words, and face hard choices without the benefit of their own history.
significance: This article explores how AI can become a cognitive symbiont, augmenting human memory, attention, and decision-making.

title: Quantum Error Correction in Nearly Critical Toric Codes
headline: Exploring Quantum Error Correction Near Criticality in Deformed Toric Codes
tldr: We study how the transverse-field toric code protects quantum information as it approaches a phase transition, analyzing performance under independent bit-flip and phase-flip noise. Our results reveal that error-correcting capabilities degrade sharply near the critical point, offering insights for designing robust topological memories.
significance: Understanding error correction near quantum phase transitions informs the limits of topological quantum memory stability.

title: A Bayesian Optimized Biquad Filter-Burg Model for Real-Time EEG Phase Estimation
headline: Bayesian Biquad Filter-Burg Model Enhances Real-Time EEG Phase Estimation for Theta-Band
tldr: This study introduces a Bayesian-optimized Biquad Filter-Burg model that improves real-time phase estimation of stimulus-aligned transient EEG in the theta band. Compared to conventional methods, it offers higher accuracy and lower latency, making it suitable for closed-loop neuromodulation.
significance: The model provides a robust, low-latency solution for precise theta-band phase tracking, a critical component for effective closed-loop brain stimulation therapies.

title: Aligning Language Models with General Preferences: An Empirical Study of Direct Nash Optimization
headline: Aligning LLMs with General Preferences via Direct Nash Optimization for Robust Alignment
tldr: This study re-implements Direct Nash Optimization (DNO) to align language models with arbitrary preference functions, using on-policy sampling, LLM-based ratings, and a DPO-style contrastive update. Experiments show DNO-Prct achieves competitive alignment performance while remaining computationally efficient.
significance: It demonstrates a scalable, game-theoretic approach to LLM alignment that generalizes beyond reward modeling.

title: Quantum Pointwise Dimension (QUPID): An algorithm for identifying classical chaos in quantum dynamics
headline: QUPID: Quantum Algorithm Detects Classical Chaos via Pointwise Dimension Analysis
tldr: QUPID is a quantum algorithm that identifies classical chaotic behavior by computing the pointwise dimension of trajectories in phase space. It distinguishes regular motion confined to invariant tori from chaotic motion that fills higher-dimensional subsets.
significance: This method bridges quantum dynamics and classical chaos theory, enabling precise diagnostics of chaotic regimes in quantum systems.

title: GUILD: Guided Iterative Data Collection for Imitation Learning
headline: GUILD: Guided Iterative Data Collection Boosts Imitation Learning in Robotics
tldr: GUILD introduces a guided, iterative approach to collect teleoperation data, focusing on high-impact samples. This method dramatically improves policy performance while reducing costly real-world data collection.
significance: By strategically curating data, GUILD enables more efficient training of robotic policies, cutting down on expensive teleoperation time.

title: A wider state, not wider arithmetic, for single-precision time integration
headline: Single-Precision Time Integration: Reducing Memory, Speeding Computations, and Managing Rounding Errors
tldr: Using single-precision floating point halves memory usage and can accelerate time integration on accelerators. A modified equation analysis separates rounding errors from truncation, enabling reliable high-performance simulations.
significance: This approach allows large-scale simulations to run faster and more efficiently without sacrificing accuracy in the stored state.

title: Designing an Adaptive Robust and Evolutionary-Game Framework for Minimum Shipment Quotas in Capacity-Constrained Freight Markets
headline: Adaptive Robust Framework for Minimum Shipment Quotas in Capacity-Constrained Freight Markets
tldr: This paper introduces an adaptive, robust, evolutionary-game framework that relaxes deterministic assumptions in minimum shipment quota regulation, allowing for dynamic market knowledge and convergence to equilibrium. The model improves allocation fairness for socially critical commodities in capacity-constrained freight markets.
significance: It provides a more realistic and flexible regulatory tool that can adapt to market uncertainty and promote equitable access to essential goods.

title: Visibility-Aware Reference Generation for Benchmarking Visual 3D Reconstruction in Vegetation-Rich Environments
headline: LiDAR-Based Reference Generation for Benchmarking 3D Reconstruction in Dense Vegetation
tldr: We introduce a LiDAR-based pipeline that automatically generates geometric ground truth for evaluating visual 3D reconstruction and depth estimation in vegetation-rich outdoor scenes. This method enables zero-shot benchmarking of feed-forward visual-geometry models and traditional SfM approaches without costly full-scanner surveys.
significance: Providing accurate, low-cost ground truth in challenging vegetation environments accelerates development and comparison of 3D reconstruction algorithms.

title: Pixel-UMI: Learning Environment-Aware Whole-Body Manipulation from Sensorized Human Demonstrations
headline: Pixel-UMI: Learning Environment-Aware Whole-Body Manipulation from Sensorized Human Demonstrations for Mobile Robots
tldr: Pixel-UMI introduces a pipeline that uses sensorized human demonstrations to train whole-body manipulation policies that adapt to the environment. By combining reconstructed scene geometry with head and gripper trajectories, the system retargets human motions to a robot while preserving task relevance and safety.
significance: This work bridges the gap between human demonstration data and robot embodiment, enabling scalable, environment-aware manipulation without manual labeling.

title: Pixel: A Co-Designed Full-Stack Robot System for Learning General-Purpose Mobile Manipulation
headline: Pixel: A Co-Designed Full-Stack System for Learning General-Purpose Mobile Manipulation
tldr: Pixel integrates robot hardware, demonstration collection, whole-body control, and policy learning into a unified system. This co-design approach eliminates mismatches and enables robust general-purpose mobile manipulation.
significance: Pixel demonstrates that tightly coupled hardware-software co-design can unlock scalable, real-world mobile manipulation capabilities.

title: EgoActionBench: Benchmarking Dense Action Captioning for Egocentric Human Videos
headline: EgoActionBench: A New Dataset Benchmark for Fine-Grained Egocentric Action Captioning
tldr: EgoActionBench provides a richly annotated, temporally precise dataset for dense action captioning from first-person videos, addressing gaps in atomic action granularity and hand-action association. The benchmark enables evaluation of models on continuous manipulation tasks with fine-grained temporal boundaries.
significance: It advances embodied AI by offering a comprehensive testbed for understanding human manipulation in egocentric contexts.

title: Single-visit screening for intracochlear tissue growth validated against multi-visit electrical measurement changes
headline: Single-Visit Screening Detects Cochlear Implant Tissue Growth Using SCINSEV Measurements
tldr: A new algorithm can identify significant tissue growth around cochlear implant electrodes from a single SCINSEV recording. The method was validated against multi-visit impedance changes, enabling early intervention without additional visits.
significance: This approach allows clinicians to monitor implant health in a single appointment, potentially improving patient outcomes and reducing healthcare costs.

title: A hyperbolic nonlinear Schrödinger system in multiple spatial dimensions: structure, convergence, and numerical discretization
headline: Hyperbolic Approximation of N-Dimensional Nonlinear Schrödinger Equation: Structure, Convergence, and Discretization
tldr: We introduce a first-order hyperbolic system that approximates the N-dimensional nonlinear Schrödinger equation, preserving key conservation laws. Numerical experiments confirm convergence and efficient real-time discretization.
significance: This work provides a mathematically rigorous, computationally efficient framework for simulating high-dimensional NLS dynamics, bridging theory and practice.

title: From Natural Language to Exact Cover: A Neuro-Symbolic Approach to Zebra Puzzles
headline: Neuro-Symbolic Exact Cover for Zebra Puzzles: Bridging LLM Reasoning and Symbolic Logic
tldr: This paper introduces a neuro-symbolic method that translates natural language zebra puzzles into exact cover problems, enabling deterministic solutions. By combining chain‑of‑thought LLMs with symbolic solvers, the approach overcomes LLMs’ logical gaps while preserving speed.
significance: It demonstrates that integrating neural reasoning with symbolic exact cover yields reliable, sound solutions for classic logic puzzles, setting a new benchmark for explainable AI.

title: Construction of the 2D non-Abelian Yang-Mills-Higgs measure via stochastic quantisation
headline: Mathematically Constructing the 2D Non-Abelian Yang-Mills-Higgs Measure via Stochastic Quantisation
tldr: We present the first rigorous construction of the non-Abelian Yang-Mills-Higgs measure on a two-dimensional torus using Parisi–Wu stochastic quantisation. By developing a gauge-covariant paracontrolled calculus, we overcome non-Markovian challenges and establish the measure’s existence.
significance: This work establishes a foundational framework for non-Abelian gauge theories in two dimensions, bridging stochastic analysis and quantum field theory.

title: Quantum channel tomography: optimal bounds in the near-boundary regime
headline: Optimal Bounds for Quantum Channel Tomography Near the Boundary Regime
tldr: This paper establishes tight optimal bounds for learning quantum channels with Kraus rank r in the near-boundary regime, where the dilation rate τ is close to one. It improves sample complexity guarantees and provides new insights into efficient quantum process tomography.
significance: It advances the theoretical limits of quantum process tomography, enabling more efficient characterization of quantum devices.

title: Mercury (Hg): a relativistic $N$-body simulation for Horndeski gravity
headline: Mercury: Relativistic N-Body Simulation for Horndeski Gravity in Cosmology and Structure Formation
tldr: Mercury is a relativistic N‑body code that extends particle‑mesh methods to include the scalar degree of freedom in Horndeski gravity. It solves the modified Einstein equations with time‑dependent α functions, enabling accurate cosmological simulations of modified gravity scenarios.
significance: Mercury provides the first fully relativistic N‑body framework for Horndeski gravity, allowing precise tests of modified gravity against cosmological observations.

title: Pretraining Data Scale Reverses the Muon-AdamW Fine-Tuning Gap
headline: Muon’s Pretraining Edge Vanishes After Fine‑Tuning for Large Datasets
tldr: Muon optimizer accelerates pretraining loss minimization compared to AdamW, but when fine‑tuned on downstream tasks, AdamW eventually outperforms Muon once the pretraining data exceeds a threshold. This suggests that Muon’s advantage is limited to pretraining and may not translate to real‑world fine‑tuning performance.
significance: Understanding when Muon’s speed advantage translates to downstream gains informs optimizer choice for large‑scale language model training pipelines.

title: Supporting Viewpoint Coordination for Compliance by Design with an Artifact Model for Regulatory Requirements Engineering
headline: Integrating Legal Expertise into Compliance-by-Design via Artifact Models for Requirements Engineering
tldr: This paper proposes an artifact model that captures regulatory requirements and supports compliance-by-design in software engineering. By involving legal experts and leveraging LLMs, the approach facilitates requirement derivation and downstream implementation.
significance: It bridges the gap between legal knowledge and software design, enabling systematic compliance integration.
